facts.fact: The Africa Report says Wave, a non-bank non-telecom operator, already holds an e-money issuer licence from the BCEAO in Senegal.

Le Soleil reports PI-SPI becomes the mandatory route for interoperable e-money transactions in the eight UEMOA states from 2 November 2026, so Senegal's banks suspended Bank to Wallet and Wallet to Bank.

The BCEAO's mandate that all interoperable electronic-money transfers across the eight WAEMU states route through PI-SPI took effect on 2 November 2026, with transfer fees capped at 0.8 per cent above 8,000 CFA francs, according to Launch Base Africa.

The BCEAO set a regulatory deadline of 30 September 2026 for institutions to connect to PI-SPI and mandated routing of interoperable e-money transfers through it from 2 November 2026; Wave, which holds about 80 per cent of Senegal's mobile money market, connected on 30 September.
BiFinances says the BCEAO set 30 June 2026 as the deadline for institutions to finish connecting to PI-SPI and provide effective service to customers, and asked those in testing to speed up.

facts.fact: The BCEAO licenses electronic money institutions in Senegal; Senegal had three at 31 December 2024 (Wave Digital Finance, Mobile Cash, Orange Finance Mobiles Senegal) per Agence Ecofin.

The BCEAO licensed the fintech Quickpay, a subsidiary of Edkoil group, as an electronic money institution from 3 March 2025, following Wave Digital Finance in April 2022, described as a non-bank, non-telecom licensee.

BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 of 23 January 2024 governs payment services across UMOA and requires providers to be licensed, with the compliance deadline extended to 31 August 2025, per Agence Ecofin.
The instruction obliges fintechs to hold a licence, with capital of 10 to 100 million FCFA, and four providers were licensed in Senegal by 27 May 2025.
BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 of 23 January 2024 requires payment service providers in WAEMU to hold a licence after a transition that ended 1 May 2025, per Ecofin Agency.
The BCEAO licensed PayDunya and Bictorys as payment institutions, Mikaty and Flutterwave Senegal as payment service providers and InTouch as an e-money institution in Senegal.
BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 of 23 January 2024 governs payment services in UMOA, and from 1 September 2025 only licensed entities may provide them, per Agence Ecofin via Digital Mag.
The instruction licenses fintechs with capital of 10 to 100 million FCFA, and four providers were licensed in Senegal by 27 May 2025.
